I'm working on a Markdown parser and I've noticed that headings and horizontal rules inside blockquotes are not being parsed correctly. * The `force_relex_at_line_start` method must be added to `BufferedLexer` in `crates/biome_parser/src/lexer.rs`. It must accept a lexer context parameter and return a syntax kind. It re-lexes the current token at the same source position while treating the position as if it were at the start of a line (i.e., as if `after_newline` / `after_line_break` is true), overriding whatever the lexer's current state says. * When a `BufferedLexer` wrapping a `MarkdownLexer` has consumed blockquote prefix tokens (`>` and a space) and is positioned at `---`, calling `force_relex_at_line_start(MarkdownLexContext::Regular)` must return `MD_THEMATIC_BREAK_LITERAL` (not `MINUS`). After the call, `current()` must also return `MD_THEMATIC_BREAK_LITERAL`. * The Markdown parser must correctly parse a setext heading inside a blockquote. Input `> Foo\n> ---\n` must produce HTML `
\n

Foo

\n
\n` and must be represented in the AST as `MdSetextHeader` with `underline_token: MD_SETEXT_UNDERLINE_LITERAL`. * The Markdown parser must correctly parse a setext heading with equals-sign underline inside a blockquote. Input `> Bar\n> ===\n` must produce an `MdSetextHeader` node with `underline_token: MD_SETEXT_UNDERLINE_LITERAL` (the `===` token). * Setext headings inside nested blockquotes must be parsed correctly. Input `> > Nested\n> > ---\n` must produce a nested `MdSetextHeader` with `underline_token: MD_SETEXT_UNDERLINE_LITERAL`. * A standalone thematic break inside a blockquote must be parsed as a thematic break, not a paragraph. Input `> ---\n` must produce HTML `
\n

code\n

This allows the parser to obtain line-start-gated tokens (such as thematic break literals) after consuming a blockquote prefix that left `after_line_break` as false. 3	//! # CommonMark Specification References
4	//!
5	//! This module implements CommonMark 0.31.2 block structure:
6	//!
7	//! ## Leaf Blocks (§4)
8	//! - **§4.1 Thematic breaks**: `---`, `***`, `___`
9	//! - **§4.2 ATX headings**: `# Heading`, `## Heading`, etc.
10	//! - **§4.3 Setext headings**: Underlined with `===` or `---`
11	//! - **§4.4 Indented code blocks**: 4+ spaces of indentation
12	//! - **§4.5 Fenced code blocks**: ``` or ~~~ delimited
13	//! - **§4.6 HTML blocks**: Raw HTML content
14	//! - **§4.7 Link reference definitions**: `[label]: url "title"`
15	//! - **§4.8 Paragraphs**: Default block content
16	//!
17	//! ## Container Blocks (§5)
18	//! - **§5.1 Block quotes**: `>` prefixed content
19	//! - **§5.2 List items**: `-`, `*`, `+` or `1.` prefixed
20	//! - **§5.3 Lists**: Sequences of list items

84	/// Result of updating parenthesis depth when scanning link destinations.
85	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
86	pub(crate) enum ParenDepthResult {
87	    /// Depth updated successfully, contains new depth value
88	    Ok(i32),
89	    /// Depth would exceed the maximum (too many nested opening parens).
90	    /// Per cmark, this truncates the destination at this point.
91	    DepthExceeded,
92	    /// Unmatched closing paren (would go below 0).
93	    /// This typically means the `)` belongs to the enclosing construct.
94	    UnmatchedClose,
95	}
96	
97	pub(crate) fn try_update_paren_depth(text: &str, depth: i32, max: i32) -> ParenDepthResult {
98	    let mut depth = depth;
99	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
100	
101	    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
102	        if c == '\\' && matches!(chars.peek(), Some('(' | ')')) {
103	            chars.next();
104	            continue;
105	        }
106	
107	        if c == '(' {
108	            if depth == max {
109	                return ParenDepthResult::DepthExceeded;
110	            }
111	            depth += 1;
112	        } else if c == ')' {
113	            if depth == 0 {
114	                return ParenDepthResult::UnmatchedClose;
115	            }
116	            depth -= 1;
117	        }
118	    }
119	
120	    ParenDepthResult::Ok(depth)
121	}

129	    text: &str,
130	    kind: LinkDestinationKind,
131	    pending_escape: &mut bool,
132	) -> bool {
133	    for c in text.chars() {
134	        if *pending_escape {
135	            if c.is_ascii_punctuation() {
136	                *pending_escape = false;
137	                continue;
138	            }
139	            *pending_escape = false;
140	        }
141	
142	        if c == '\\' {
143	            *pending_escape = true;
144	            continue;
145	        }
146	
147	        if c.is_ascii_control() {
148	            return false;
149	        }
150	
151	        if matches!(kind, LinkDestinationKind::Enclosed) && c == '<' {
152	            return false;
153	        }
154	    }
155	
156	    true
157	}

159	pub(crate) fn ends_with_unescaped_close(text: &str, close_char: char) -> bool {
160	    if !text.ends_with(close_char) {
161	        return false;
162	    }
163	
164	    let mut backslashes = 0;
165	    for c in text.chars().rev().skip(1) {
166	        if c == '\\' {
167	            backslashes += 1;
168	        } else {
169	            break;
170	        }
171	    }
172	
173	    backslashes % 2 == 0
174	}

All changes are in place and verified. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Summary

The root cause: after the Markdown lexer consumes a blockquote prefix (`>` + optional space), its `after_line_break` flag is `false`, so line-start-gated tokens were mis-lexed — `---` became `MINUS` tokens, `___`/`***` became `DOUBLE_*` tokens, and `===` became textual. This prevented the parser from recognizing thematic breaks (§4.1) and setext underlines (§4.3) inside blockquotes.

### Changes

**1. `crates/biome_parser/src/lexer.rs`** — Added `BufferedLexer::force_relex_at_line_start(context) -> Lex::Kind`. It rewinds the inner lexer to the current token's start, forces `after_line_break: true`, clears the lookahead cache, re-lexes in the given context, and updates `current` (so `current()` returns the new kind). Mirrors the existing `force_relex_in_context` but overrides the line-break state.

**2. `crates/biome_markdown_parser/src/token_source.rs`** & **`parser.rs`** — Threaded the method through `MarkdownTokenSource` and exposed a parser-level `force_relex_at_line_start()` (Regular context).

**3. `crates/biome_markdown_parser/src/syntax/quote.rs`**:
- After consuming a quote prefix in `emit_quote_prefix_tokens`, call `relex_break_after_quote_prefix`, which re-lexes the following token at line start **only** when it's `-`, `*`, `_`, `__`, or a `=`-leading textual token. `**`-runs (`DOUBLE_STAR`, e.g. `> ***`) are deliberately excluded so those stay paragraphs per the spec given. Because this is the single chokepoint for both first-line prefixes and continuation-line prefixes (via `consume_quote_prefix_impl`), it fixes standalone breaks, list-shaped breaks, and setext continuations uniformly.
- Fixed `parse_code_block_newline` to check via lookahead whether the next line still continues the indented code block **before** consuming its quote prefix, so a following thematic break line ends the code block cleanly instead of absorbing `> ` into code content.

### Verification
A scratch harness confirmed all 11 required behaviors (HTML + AST: 6 `MdThematicBreakBlock`, 3 `MdSetextHeader` with `MD_SETEXT_UNDERLINE_LITERAL`, and the two paragraph carve-outs). The full `biome_markdown_parser` suite passes except one pre-existing snapshot (`setext_heading_edge_cases.md`) which now correctly parses `> Foo\n> ---` as a setext heading — exactly the mandated new behavior; its `.snap` lives under `tests/` and will be updated by the verification patch. `biome_parser` tests and dependent parser crates build/pass.

One note: I left `tests/` untouched per your instruction, so the `setext_heading_edge_cases.md.snap` will show as failing until the verification patch updates it to the new (correct) expected output.
